boundaries.comunidades_sfha.plain: How much of the community's land lies inside a FEMA Special Flood Hazard Area, the area with a 1% chance of flooding in any year (the 100-year flood), as a percent and in km².
boundaries.comunidades_sfha.plain_es: Qué parte del terreno de la comunidad está dentro de un Área Especial de Riesgo de Inundación (SFHA) de FEMA (Agencia Federal para el Manejo de Emergencias), el área con 1% de probabilidad de inundarse en cualquier año (la inundación de 100 años), como porcentaje y en km².
boundaries.comunidades_sfha.definition: sfha_pct is the area of the community polygon that falls inside any FEMA National Flood Hazard Layer polygon with SFHA_TF = 'T' (zones A, AE, AH, AO, A99, V and VE), divided by the community's area, times 100. sfha_km2 is km2 × sfha_pct ÷ 100. In the 2026-10 build, 248 of the 713 communities have some area in the SFHA, 95 have half or more, and 49 lie entirely inside it (99.5% or more); together 19.70 km² of community land is inside the SFHA.
boundaries.comunidades_sfha.method: comunidades.py intersects the full-detail community polygon with the full-detail SFHA polygons (not the simplified copies the maps draw), merges the overlapping pieces so no area counts twice, and divides by the community's area. Both areas are measured in degrees², which over one community gives the same ratio as true areas. km² uses the Junta's Shape_Area, so sfha_km2 and km2 agree. A check against the simplified map copy of the flood zones, measured in kilometers, differs by more than 1 percentage point for 8 communities, at most 3.7 points (on a 0.03 km² community).
boundaries.comunidades_sfha.how_to_read: A value of 100% means the whole community is in the mapped 1% annual chance flood area; 0% means none of it is. Combine it with housing units for a rough sense of how many homes may sit in the flood area, keeping in mind that homes are not spread evenly inside a community.
caveats: Describes the mapped hazard on the land, not the elevation, construction or insurance of any home.
The 0.2% annual chance (500-year) zone and areas FEMA has not mapped are not counted.
The outlines are from 2006 and the flood maps are more recent, so a community that grew beyond its 2006 outline is measured only inside it.
boundaries.comunidades_sfha.source_detail: FEMA NFHL MapServer layer 28, DFIRM_ID LIKE '72%', SFHA_TF = 'T' (2,517 polygons); the same download build.py uses (cache/fema_nfhl_pr.geojson)

boundaries.comunidades_especiales.plain: The outlines of the 713 communities designated for the Comunidades Especiales program under Ley 1-2001, as the Planning Board (Junta de Planificación) drew them in 2006. Each has its name, municipality, barrio and area.
boundaries.comunidades_especiales.plain_es: Los contornos de las 713 comunidades designadas para el programa de Comunidades Especiales bajo la Ley 1-2001, según los trazó la Junta de Planificación (JP) en 2006. Cada una tiene su nombre, municipio, barrio y área.
boundaries.comunidades_especiales.definition: The file comunidades.geojson holds one shape per community from the Junta de Planificación's 2006 delimitation of the Comunidades Especiales. 620 shapes are one polygon and 93 have several parts. The observatory keeps the name (nombre), municipality (municipio), barrio, area in km² (km2) and four inventory fields and two flood measures, each documented in its own entry.
boundaries.comunidades_especiales.method: comunidades.py pages the public copy of the layer, checks that every municipality name matches the observatory's list, simplifies each shape for display (tolerance 0.00005 degrees, about 5 m) and rounds coordinates to 5 decimals. Barrio names are changed from capitals to title case. km2 is the layer's Shape_Area (square meters in the Junta's State Plane projection) divided by 1,000,000, so it is measured on the original shape.
boundaries.comunidades_especiales.how_to_read: Turn the layer on and click inside a community for its name, housing units, type and the hazards residents reported. Turn on the flood zones too to see which communities sit in a mapped flood area today.
caveats: A 2006 delimitation. Communities designated later may be missing, and some outlines may no longer match what is on the ground.
Names come from the layer as written. The barrio is the Junta's attribute and is not checked against the Census barrios the observatory draws.

essentials.ess_supermarket_far_pct.plain: The share of residents who live more than 5 km by road from the nearest supermarket.
essentials.ess_supermarket_far_pct.plain_es: La proporción de residentes que viven a más de 5 km por carretera del supermercado más cercano.
essentials.ess_supermarket_far_pct.definition: The share of the area's residents (2020 Census) who live more than 5 km by road from the nearest supermarket. Supermarkets are Overture's grocery and warehouse-club places whose name is a supermarket's ("supermercado", "supermarket" or a supermarket chain), plus Walmart, Costco and Sam's Club, and OpenStreetMap's supermarkets that Overture lacks; corner stores (colmados) are left out. An estimate: distance along the mapped roads in either direction, not a driving route or a time. The places come from a directory, so a shop that closed may still be counted and one that opened may be missing. Blocks with no road within 2 km, or no road to any place of the kind, are left out.
essentials.ess_supermarket_far_pct.method: essentials.py searches the road graph the map uses (roads.bin, from OpenStreetMap) outward from every place of a kind at once, in both directions of every road (one-way streets are read as two-way: a distance, not a driving route). Each 2020 Census block with residents is snapped to the nearest road joined to the network within 2 km; its distance is the road distance to the nearest place, plus the straight lines from the block and the place to their roads. A barrio's or municipio's figure is the average over its residents. Shops come from Overture's places (confidence 0.5 or more) and OpenStreetMap's that Overture lacks; libraries and fire stations from the map's own layers, with OpenStreetMap's fire stations that USGS lacks. No time is estimated and no traffic is assumed.
essentials.ess_supermarket_far_pct.how_to_read: Puerto Rico: 16.0%. Highest: Maricao (100.0%), Comerío (85.7%), Yabucoa (62.4%). From Overture's places alone, 17.4%.
caveats: The places come from directories, not an inspection: a shop that closed may still be listed (the distance then reads shorter) and one that opened may be missing (longer).
5 km is the observatory's line, about 3 miles; the USDA's food-access atlas uses 1 mile in towns and 10 in the country, and leaves Puerto Rico out.
A road distance, not a travel time: it does not say whether people have a car, how often a bus passes or how steep the road is.
essentials.ess_supermarket_far_pct.source_detail: Estimated by the observatory: road distance over the OpenStreetMap road graph (roads.bin) from each 2020 Census block with residents to the nearest point of the kind, averaged over residents (essentials.py)

layers.historic_places.plain: Places listed on the National Register of Historic Places, with their name, type, municipio and the date they were listed. Private homes and haciendas are counted by municipio, not drawn.
layers.historic_places.plain_es: Los lugares inscritos en el Registro Nacional de Lugares Históricos, con su nombre, tipo, municipio y la fecha en que se inscribieron. Las residencias y haciendas privadas se cuentan por municipio, pero no aparecen en el mapa.
layers.historic_places.definition: historic_places.geojson: one point per listing and municipio from the National Park Service's public locations (a listing with only an outline is placed at a point inside it), with name, type (historic building, structure, district, site or object), municipio, geoid and listed (the listing date, YYYY-MM or YYYY-MM-DD). Private residences, and listings whose name holds a street address or house number, are not drawn: they count in nrhp_places, and the file's notes give how many by municipio (counted_not_drawn_by_municipio). 277 points for 269 of 342 listings on 2026-10-18; 73 listings counted only.
layers.historic_places.method: community_assets.py reads layers 0 and 1 of the NPS service for Puerto Rico, keeps listed properties, places each point by point in polygon and keeps one point per listing and municipio. The address is never requested. NPS gives no ownership or use field: names that match a pattern (Casa, House, Residencia, Residence, Home, Villa, Chalet, Quinta, Hacienda, a number or a street word) are reviewed by hand in nrhp_review.json, which keeps public buildings, museums, public heritage sites and numbered bridges drawn and counts private residences only (decided by FPR on 2026-10-18). The 2D map (facilities.js) and the 3D view (facilities3d.js) draw it with core/facilities.js, which holds its file, color, pop-up and note.
layers.historic_places.how_to_read: Switch the layer on in the Map layers tab of the 2D map or the 3D view (Community services, Education and culture: Historic places). Both views draw the same points, with the same note on what is counted but not drawn and the same pop-up. Click a point for the place's name, type, municipio, listing date and source.
caveats: Points can be off by tens of meters, and a listing may no longer stand.

Private homes are counted, not drawn, and their names are not published; the review is by name and public descriptions, so a few borderline buildings (listed in nrhp_review.json) may be on the wrong side.
Sensitive listings, such as archaeological sites, are not public.

community.nrhp_places.plain: How many places in each municipio are listed on the National Register of Historic Places, the federal list of buildings, sites and districts worth preserving.
community.nrhp_places.plain_es: Cuántos lugares de cada municipio están inscritos en el Registro Nacional de Lugares Históricos, la lista federal de edificios, sitios y distritos que merecen conservarse.
community.nrhp_places.definition: Buildings, structures, sites, objects and historic districts of Puerto Rico listed on the National Register of Historic Places, in the municipio that holds each listing's point (National Park Service public locations). A listing with points in several municipios counts in each; Puerto Rico's value counts each listing once. Every listing counts, private residences too (73 on 2026-10-18, privately owned haciendas and a former home for the elderly among them), although the map does not draw those. Restricted and sensitive listings, such as archaeological sites, are not in the public data.
community.nrhp_places.method: community_assets.py reads the National Park Service's public locations service for Puerto Rico: 360 points (layer 0) and, for the 14 listings with only an outline, a point inside the outline (layer 1). Each point is placed in the municipio that holds it; the two points at sea (a lighthouse on a cay, a crash site) go to the municipio their listing's city names, and one point of an irrigation system that falls in the sea is left out. A listing counts once in each municipio where it has a point. 342 listings on 2026-10-18, of which 73 are private residences, privately owned haciendas, a home for the elderly when listed, or are named by a street address (counted, not drawn; historic_places.geojson notes.counted_not_drawn_by_municipio gives them by municipio).
community.nrhp_places.how_to_read: Puerto Rico has 342 listings: San Juan 66, Ponce 45, Mayagüez 17, Arecibo 16. Four municipios have none. The municipal values add up to more than Puerto Rico's because a historic road or irrigation system counts in each municipio it crosses.
caveats: A listing is a federal recognition, not a measure of all heritage: many historic places were never nominated, and Puerto Rico's own register (Instituto de Cultura Puertorriqueña, Junta de Planificación) is not included.
Most points come from the nomination's coordinates and can be off by tens of meters; NPS says the data are for general reference only.
A listing may no longer stand: NPS marks most Puerto Rico points 'existence unknown'.
community.nrhp_places.source_detail: NPS nrhp_locations MapServer, layers 0 and 1, State = 'PUERTO RICO'; fields NRIS_Refnum, RESNAME, ResType, City, CertDate, STATUS

layers.town_halls.plain: City halls (alcaldías) as volunteers mapped them in OpenStreetMap, with their name, type and municipio.
layers.town_halls.plain_es: Las alcaldías tal como las trazaron los voluntarios de OpenStreetMap, con su nombre, tipo y municipio.
layers.town_halls.definition: town_halls.geojson: one point per OpenStreetMap feature tagged amenity=townhall (a building outline is drawn at its center), with name (3 have none), type (city hall, or city hall annex when the name says Anexo), municipio, geoid and osm (the OpenStreetMap element, such as w123). 65 features on 2026-10-18: 63 city halls in 62 municipios and 2 annexes.
layers.town_halls.method: community_assets.py asks the Overpass API for every amenity=townhall node, way and relation in Puerto Rico's bounding box and places each by point in polygon. A node and its building with the same name within 30 m would count once (none on 2026-10-18). The 2D map (facilities.js) and the 3D view (facilities3d.js) draw it with core/facilities.js, which holds its file, color, pop-up and note.
layers.town_halls.how_to_read: Switch the layer on in the Map layers tab of the 2D map or the 3D view (Community services, Government: City halls). Both views draw the same points, with the same note on what is counted but not drawn and the same pop-up. 16 municipios have no city hall mapped on 2026-10-18 (Adjuntas, Aguas Buenas, Arroyo, Barceloneta, Barranquitas, Cidra, Coamo, Florida, Guayama, Hormigueros, Juana Díaz, Juncos, Orocovis, Quebradillas, Río Grande and San Sebastián). Every municipio has a city hall; the gap is in the map, and anyone can add one at openstreetmap.org.
caveats: Volunteers map these; 16 municipios have none mapped, and none was added by hand.
ODbL: credit OpenStreetMap contributors; a database built on this file must be shared alike.

wcrp.ce_assets.plain: Whether each Comunidad Especial had a community center, a library, an electronic library, a passive park, a sports court, a residents', recreation or crime-prevention association, and a PDI, as the WCRP Social Capital Mapping list records it; counted by municipio.
wcrp.ce_assets.plain_es: Si cada Comunidad Especial tenía centro comunal, biblioteca, biblioteca electrónica, parque pasivo, cancha, asociación de residentes, recreativa o de prevención del crimen, y PDI, según la lista de Mapeo de Capital Social de WCRP; contado por municipio.
wcrp.ce_assets.definition: Nine Yes/No flags of the WCRP Social Capital Mapping list of 711 Comunidades Especiales, as the list writes them: centro_comunal (community center), biblioteca (library), biblioteca_electronica (electronic library), parque_pasivo (passive park), cancha (sports court), asoc_residentes (residents' association), asoc_recreativa (recreation association), asoc_prevencion_crimen (crime-prevention association) and pdi (the list's column PDI, which it does not define). Each flag is 'si', 'no' or 'nd' ('Información No Disponible'). By municipio and for Puerto Rico: listed (rows of the list), matched (rows matched to a polygon of comunidades.geojson), yes.<flag> (rows with 'si') and unknown.<flag> (rows with 'nd'); and for each matched polygon its nine flags as one code (1 yes, 0 no, - not recorded).
wcrp.ce_assets.method: wcrp_social.py --import reads the list, restores the municipio names and, where it can, the accented letters the copy lost, and matches each row to a polygon of the same municipio: by the same name once accents, capitals and punctuation are set aside (686 rows), by name and barrio where two polygons share the name (1), or by a clearly closest name in the same barrio (23; listed with enlace = parecido in wcrp_ce_assets.csv for review). One row is not matched (Parcelas Pda. 27, San Juan); 3 polygons have no row. The build counts the flags by municipio over every row, matched or not.
wcrp.ce_assets.how_to_read: Read a count as what the list recorded when it was compiled, not as today's situation. 'Not recorded' is not 'no': about 110 to 130 rows have no information for each flag except PDI.
caveats: The list's date is not stated. It was compiled for the WCRP Social Capital Mapping tool, about 2019-2021, from the Junta de Planificación inventory; assets may have opened or closed since.
The list does not define PDI.
23 rows are matched to a polygon by a close name, not the same name: wcrp_ce_assets.csv marks them (enlace = parecido) so a reviewer can check them.

wcrp.social_counts.plain: For each municipio: its residents (latest Census Bureau estimate), which the WCRP page divides the asset counts by, and how many Comunidades Especiales and housing units in them it has (2006).
wcrp.social_counts.plain_es: Para cada municipio: sus residentes (el estimado más reciente del Negociado del Censo), entre los que la página de WCRP divide los conteos de activos, y cuántas Comunidades Especiales y unidades de vivienda en ellas tiene (2006).
wcrp.social_counts.definition: population: residents, the latest year of the Census Bureau's Population Estimates in housing_series.json (2025, Vintage 2025), the denominator of the per-1,000 rates of the WCRP page's municipio summary. polygons: the Comunidades Especiales of comunidades.geojson in the municipio. housing_units: the sum of their housing units (viviendas, Junta de Planificación 2006 inventory). The last value of each array is Puerto Rico.
wcrp.social_counts.method: Copied from housing_series.json (population, latest year) and counted from comunidades.geojson by its municipio field. The residents inside a protected area, which the summary divides by the 2020 Census residents, come from exposure_municipio.json.
wcrp.social_counts.how_to_read: A rate per 1,000 residents compares municipios of different sizes; for small counts (a few stations) a single facility moves the rate a lot.
caveats: The Comunidades Especiales and their housing units describe the 2006 delimitation, not today.

boundaries.wcrp_comunidades.plain: The communities that are writing or have written a resilience plan in FPR's Whole Community Resilience Planning (WCRP) program. Each one is a single dot near the community, with its name, municipality and WCRP region.
boundaries.wcrp_comunidades.plain_es: Las comunidades que preparan o ya prepararon un plan de resiliencia en el programa Whole Community Resilience Planning (WCRP) de FPR. Cada una aparece como un solo punto cerca de la comunidad, con su nombre, municipio y región de WCRP.
boundaries.wcrp_comunidades.definition: The file wcrp.geojson holds one point per community in the WCRP program list of 2026-10-06: 76 communities in 30 municipalities. Several plans can share one point (73 different points), for example Villa Calma 1 and 2. The observatory keeps the community name (comunidad), municipality (municipio) and WCRP region (region: norte, este, sur, central, oeste or islas; empty for the 4 communities that no source assigns to a region), and three fields documented in their own entries.
boundaries.wcrp_comunidades.method: wcrp.py reads wcrp_comunidades.csv: 72 rows from the WCRP-RAG list and 7 phase-1 communities from FPR's Smartsheet tracker, which the WCRP-RAG does not list yet. For each row without a point it looks, in the same municipality, for a Comunidad Especial with a similar name, then an OpenStreetMap place with the same name, then a Census barrio with the same name; Centro Urbano and Casco Urbano plans go to the town center. FPR placed the other 29 by hand, from what each plan says about its location or, for communities without a plan yet, from the program's tracker; the CSV cites the source. The script checks that every point lies within about 100 m of its municipality.
boundaries.wcrp_comunidades.how_to_read: Use it to see where the program works and to compare with other layers, such as flood zones or the Comunidades Especiales. Do not read the dot as the community's boundary or its center.
caveats: Each dot is approximate. The plans draw the community's area only in a PDF map, so the observatory has no outlines yet.

Three plans of the program serve a population group, not an area (people without a home in Ponce, and immigrant and vulnerable populations in Río Piedras). They are not on the map: on 2026-11-23 FPR decided that groups of people are not shown as points on a public map.
One community, Ceiba Carmelita, also reaches into Vega Baja; its dot is in Vega Alta.
El Cerro (Naranjito) has a provisional point at the town center: no source gives its location yet.
boundaries.wcrp_comunidades.geography: 76 communities in 30 municipalities: 28 in the norte region, 17 este, 12 sur, 10 central, 4 oeste, 1 islas and 4 without a region
boundaries.wcrp_comunidades.source_detail: wcrp_comunidades.csv (columns comunidad, municipio, region); comunidades.geojson and gazetteer.json for the points

wcrp.rvi_age_context.plain: The share of each barrio's residents in four age groups (under 18, 18 to 44, 45 to 64, 65 and over), from the Census survey of 2020–2024, shown beside the updated WCRP vulnerability index (Updated 2020–2024). They are not part of the index and change no level.
wcrp.rvi_age_context.plain_es: La proporción de los residentes de cada barrio en cuatro grupos de edad (menores de 18, de 18 a 44, de 45 a 64, de 65 o más), de la encuesta del Censo de 2020–2024, que se muestra junto al índice de vulnerabilidad WCRP actualizado (Actualizado 2020–2024). No forman parte del índice y no cambian ningún nivel.
wcrp.rvi_age_context.definition: Four fields for each of the 901 barrios, in the rebuild block's context (wcrp_rvi_inputs.json): age_under18_pct: residents under 18 (%); age_18to44_pct: residents aged 18 to 44 (%); age_45to64_pct: residents aged 45 to 64 (%); age_65plus_pct: residents aged 65 and over (%). context_moe holds the margin of error of each (90% confidence, percentage points). The original dashboard showed the same groups as counts (All_Indicator UNDER17, OVER65 and the age bands, ACS 2015–2019) beside its index as the vulnerable population; the white paper's method uses no age input (its Appendix A lists vulnerable populations among the candidates, not among the inputs chosen).
wcrp.rvi_age_context.method: Copied from acs_barrio.json (acs_under18_pct, acs_age18to44_pct, acs_age45to64_pct, acs_age65plus_pct and their margins of error, built by small_area.py from table B01001) for the rebuild's survey window, rounded to one decimal.
wcrp.rvi_age_context.how_to_read: Survey estimates for barrios are rough: the WCRP page gives each share with its margin of error. A share of 0 in a small barrio can be a sampling result, not the absence of the group.
caveats: Context only: not an input of the index, so it changes no rank.
The original's age groups (under 17, over 65) do not match these bands exactly; the page does not compare them.
wcrp.rvi_age_context.source_detail: ACS 5-year 2020–2024, table B01001 (sex by age), barrio rows: acs_barrio.json

wcrp.rvi_inputs_orig.plain: The values behind each barrio's WCRP vulnerability index in the original 2022 version, as published: poverty, public assistance, unemployment, schooling, environmental sites, disability, insurance, hospital travel time, housing and internet.
wcrp.rvi_inputs_orig.plain_es: Los valores detrás del índice de vulnerabilidad WCRP de cada barrio en la versión original de 2022, tal como se publicaron: pobreza, asistencia pública, desempleo, escolaridad, lugares ambientales, discapacidad, seguro, tiempo de viaje al hospital, vivienda e internet.
wcrp.rvi_inputs_orig.definition: One field per input, for each of the 901 barrios: o_public_assist_pct: Population on public assistance (%); o_per_capita_income: Per capita income ($; shown in the table, not an input of the index per the white paper); o_poverty_pct: Population below the poverty line (%); o_unemployed_pct: Unemployed (%); o_not_enrolled_3_24_pct: People aged 3 to 24 not enrolled in school (%); o_no_diploma_pct: Adults 25+ without a high school diploma (%); o_nonattainment: In a sulfur dioxide or lead non-attainment area (1 = yes); o_impaired_water: Impaired water body, EPA 303(d) (1 = yes); o_rmp_sites: Risk Management Plan sites (count); o_dumps: Municipal landfill or open dump (1 = yes); o_solid_waste: Solid waste facility (1 = yes); o_npl_sites: Superfund (National Priorities List) sites (count); o_tri_facilities: Toxics Release Inventory facilities (count); o_lead_paint_pct: Lead-paint indicator: homes built before 1960 (%); o_disability_pct: People with a disability (%); o_uninsured_pct: People without health insurance (%); o_hospital_min: Travel time to the nearest general hospital (minutes); o_vacancy_pct: Vacant housing units (%); o_built_pre1990_pct: Homes built before 1990 (%); o_severe_problems_pct: Severe housing problems, HUD CHAS definition (%); o_intersections_sqmi: Street intersections per square mile (TIGER 2020); o_no_vehicle_pct: Households with no vehicle (%); o_no_computer_pct: Households without a computer (%); o_no_internet_pct: Households without internet (%); o_no_broadband_pct: Households without broadband (%). population: total population (ACS 2015-2019, TOTPOP).
wcrp.rvi_inputs_orig.method: Read from the barrio columns of the public ArcGIS table Master_Data_Table_Update (Var1 to Var8 of each indicator's rows; GEOID is a number there and is matched to the observatory's ten-digit barrio code) and TOTPOP from All_Indicator. The municipio and Puerto Rico columns are not kept: several are mislabeled. The labels follow the dashboard's barrio list and the white paper. The 21 barrios with nobody aged 3 to 24 (white paper, appendix C) carry a 0 for school enrollment in the service; the observatory stores no value for them, as the white paper says.
wcrp.rvi_inputs_orig.how_to_read: These are the values the original ranked; compare them with the rebuild's inputs in the WCRP page's pop-up, keeping in mind that the two versions may define an input differently.
caveats: A rank compares barrios with each other on the inputs used. It is not a measure of need, risk of harm or eligibility for any program.

wcrp.rvi_inputs_rebuild.plain: The values behind each barrio's updated WCRP vulnerability index (Updated 2020–2024): shares from the Census survey of 2020–2024, such as poverty, unemployment, disability, vacancy and households without internet, and current counts of EPA sites, flags for impaired waters and polluted air, severe housing problems, street intersections and the drive time to a hospital.
wcrp.rvi_inputs_rebuild.plain_es: Los valores detrás del índice de vulnerabilidad WCRP actualizado de cada barrio (Actualizado 2020–2024): proporciones de la encuesta del Censo de 2020–2024, como pobreza, desempleo, discapacidad, viviendas desocupadas y hogares sin internet, y conteos actuales de lugares de la EPA, marcas de aguas deterioradas y aire contaminado, problemas graves de vivienda, intersecciones de calles y el tiempo en auto a un hospital.
wcrp.rvi_inputs_rebuild.definition: One field per input, for each of the 901 barrios: poverty_pct: People below the poverty line (%) (acs_barrio:poverty_pct); public_assist_hh_pct: Households with cash public assistance income (%) (B19057: 002 / 001); unemployment_rate_pct: Unemployment rate (%) (acs_barrio:unemployment_rate_pct); not_enrolled_3_24_pct: People aged 3 to 24 not enrolled in school (%) (B14003: not enrolled aged 3 to 24 / everyone aged 3 to 24); acs_no_hs_pct: Adults 25+ without a high school diploma (%) (acs_barrio:acs_no_hs_pct); built_pre1960_pct: Lead-paint indicator: homes built before 1960 (%) (B25034: 009 + 010 + 011 / 001); nonattainment_flag: In a sulfur dioxide or lead non-attainment area (1 = yes) (conditions_barrio: epa_naa_so2_pct > 0 or epa_naa_lead_pct > 0); impaired_water_flag: In a 303(d)-listed water assessment unit, EPA ATTAINS (1 = yes) (conditions_barrio: epa_303d_pct > 0); rmp_sites: Risk Management Plan facilities, active (count) (conditions_barrio:epa_rmp); landfill_flag: Municipal solid waste landfill, open or closed, EPA LMOP (1 = yes) (conditions_barrio: epa_landfills > 0); npl_sites: Superfund (National Priorities List) sites (count) (conditions_barrio:epa_npl); tri_facilities: Toxics Release Inventory facilities (count) (conditions_barrio:epa_tri); acs_disability_pct: People with a disability (%) (acs_barrio:acs_disability_pct); acs_uninsured_pct: People without health insurance (%) (acs_barrio:acs_uninsured_pct); hospital_drive_min: Drive time to the nearest general hospital (minutes, estimate) (conditions_barrio:hosp_drive_min); vacancy_pct: Vacant housing units (%) (acs_barrio:vacancy_pct); built_pre1990_pct: Homes built before 1990 (%) (B25034: 006 to 011 / 001); severe_problems_pct: Households with severe housing problems, CHAS 2016–2020 (%, estimate) (conditions_barrio:chas_severe_pct); no_computer_pct: Households without a computer (%) (B28003: 006 / 001); no_internet_pct: Households with no internet access (%) (acs_barrio:no_internet_pct); no_broadband_pct: Households without broadband (%) (B28002: (001 - 004) / 001); no_vehicle_hh_pct: Households with no vehicle (%) (acs_barrio:no_vehicle_hh_pct); intersection_density: Street intersections per square mile, TIGER/Line 2026 (fewer is more vulnerable) (conditions_barrio:street_intersection_density). Shares are percent; flags are 1 (yes) or 0; counts are sites in the barrio; the drive time is in minutes. The population of each version is in the population field of its block (ACS 2020–2024, acs_population).
wcrp.rvi_inputs_rebuild.method: Variables that acs_barrio.json holds are copied from its newest window; the others are computed from the barrio rows of the same window's tables read by acs_small.py: the cells named after each label. The other inputs are copied from conditions_barrio.json (conditions.py); a flag is 1 where the barrio's share of the area is above 0. A share whose denominator is zero or missing has no value. Rounded to one decimal.
wcrp.rvi_inputs_rebuild.how_to_read: Survey estimates for barrios are rough; their margins of error are in acs_barrio.json for the variables it holds and are not kept here.
caveats: Margins of error are not stored in this file.
Definitions can differ from the original's, which does not say which cells or layers it used; the WCRP page lists the inputs whose current source defines them differently.
Severe housing problems and the drive time to a hospital are estimates (see conditions.chas_severe_pct and conditions.hosp_drive_min); Vieques, Culebra and Isla de Mona have no drive time.
wcrp.rvi_inputs_rebuild.source_detail: ACS 5-year 2020–2024: acs_barrio.json; tables B19057, B25034, B28003, B28002 and B14003 (barrio rows); conditions_barrio.json (EPA TRI, FRS, ATTAINS, Green Book, LMOP; HUD CHAS 2016-2020; TIGER/Line 2026; CMS hospitals and OpenStreetMap roads)

wcrp.rvi_econ_orig.plain: How vulnerable each barrio was in economy compared with the other barrios, in the WCRP Risk and Vulnerability Indicators as published in 2022: a level from 1 (the least vulnerable fifth) to 5 (the most vulnerable fifth).
wcrp.rvi_econ_orig.plain_es: Cuán vulnerable era cada barrio en economía comparado con los demás barrios, según los Indicadores de Riesgo y Vulnerabilidad de WCRP publicados en 2022: un nivel de 1 (el quinto menos vulnerable) a 5 (el quinto más vulnerable).
wcrp.rvi_econ_orig.definition: The economy index of the Risk and Vulnerability Indicators (RVI) that Hunter College built for Foundation for Puerto Rico's Whole Community Resilience Planning (WCRP) program, as published in March 2022: the barrio's percentile among the 887 barrios with residents (0 to 1 in the source, stored times 100), where higher is more vulnerable, and its rank, the fifth of the index (1 = 0 to 20, low; 5 = above 80, high). Inputs: Population on public assistance (%); Population below the poverty line (%); Unemployed (%). Mostly ACS 2015-2019; the environment inputs are EPA layers of about 2021 and FPR-supplied waste layers, travel time to a hospital was computed by Hunter College, and intersection density uses TIGER 2020. The 14 barrios with no residents or structures have no value.
wcrp.rvi_econ_orig.method: Read as published from the public ArcGIS service All_Indicator (the OVERALL row of each barrio carries every area's index and rank); nothing is recomputed. The build checks that each published rank is the fifth of the published index (rank = ceil(5 x index), at least 1) and stops if one is not. Method of the source (white paper, December 2021): each input becomes a percentile among the barrios, the percentiles of an area are added and the sum ranked again; the overall index ranks the sum of the six area indices. Applied to the original's own published inputs, that method gives back this index with a rank correlation of 0.68 (39.1% of barrios keep their rank). Economy does not reproduce: its published inputs do not give back its published index, and the white paper does not explain why.
